records.title: MPI Message Tag
verifiedClaims: MPI point-to-point messages can carry integer tags that receivers use together with source and communicator information for message matching.

records.title: MPI Blocking Receive
verifiedClaims: A blocking MPI receive does not return until the receive buffer can be safely used by the caller according to the MPI completion semantics.

records.title: MPI Barrier
verifiedClaims: MPI_Barrier blocks participating processes until all processes in the communicator have entered the barrier.

records.title: MPI Gather
verifiedClaims: MPI_Gather collects equal-size contributions from all processes and places the combined result at the root process.

records.title: MPI Scatter
verifiedClaims: MPI_Scatter distributes distinct chunks of a root process buffer to participating processes.

records.title: MPI Collective Communication
verifiedClaims: MPI collective operations involve all processes in a communicator and provide standardized patterns such as broadcast, gather, scatter, reduce, and barrier.

records.title: Slurm Job
verifiedClaims: A Slurm job is an allocation of resources requested by a user for executing work on a managed cluster.

records.title: Slurm Partition
verifiedClaims: A Slurm partition groups nodes into a scheduling set and can carry limits and policies that affect jobs submitted to it.

records.title: Slurm sbatch
verifiedClaims: sbatch submits a batch script to Slurm and returns after the job has been accepted for scheduling.

records.title: Slurm srun
verifiedClaims: srun launches parallel or serial tasks within a Slurm allocation or can request an allocation for an interactive step.

records.title: Slurm Job Step
verifiedClaims: A Slurm job step is a set of tasks launched within a job allocation, commonly through srun.

records.title: CUDA Thread
verifiedClaims: A CUDA thread executes one instance of a kernel and has built-in indices used to determine which data it should process.

records.title: CUDA Thread Block
verifiedClaims: A CUDA thread block is a group of threads that can cooperate through shared memory and block-level synchronization.

records.title: CUDA Grid
verifiedClaims: A CUDA kernel launch organizes thread blocks into a grid.

records.title: CUDA Warp
verifiedClaims: CUDA hardware schedules threads in groups called warps; on current NVIDIA CUDA architectures a warp contains 32 threads.

records.title: CUDA Warp Divergence
verifiedClaims: Threads in a warp that take different control-flow paths can require the warp to execute those paths separately, reducing effective parallel efficiency.

records.title: CUDA Registers
verifiedClaims: CUDA registers are per-thread storage allocated from each streaming multiprocessor register file.

records.title: CUDA Constant Memory
verifiedClaims: CUDA constant memory is a read-only memory space visible to device code and backed by a cache optimized for certain access patterns.

records.title: CUDA Coalesced Global Loads
verifiedClaims: CUDA combines a warp’s global-memory accesses into the number of memory transactions needed to cover the requested address segments; efficient coalescing minimizes unnecessary transactions.

sources.title: NVIDIA — CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide

records.title: CUDA Occupancy
verifiedClaims: CUDA occupancy is the ratio of active warps on a streaming multiprocessor to the maximum active warps supported by that multiprocessor.

records.title: CUDA Register Pressure
verifiedClaims: High per-thread register use can reduce the number of resident blocks or warps that fit on a streaming multiprocessor.

records.title: CUDA Shared-Memory Pressure
verifiedClaims: High per-block shared-memory use can reduce the number of thread blocks that can reside concurrently on a streaming multiprocessor.

records.title: CUDA __syncthreads
verifiedClaims: __syncthreads() is a block-level barrier that waits until participating threads in the block reach the barrier and makes prior shared/global memory accesses visible according to CUDA synchronization semantics.

records.title: Lamport Happens-Before Relation
verifiedClaims: Lamport defines a happens-before relation that orders events when one event causally precedes another through process order or message transmission.

sources.title: Leslie Lamport — Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

records.title: Lamport Logical Clock
verifiedClaims: A Lamport logical clock assigns scalar timestamps that preserve happens-before ordering: if event a happens before event b, then the clock value of a is smaller than the clock value of b.

sources.title: Leslie Lamport — Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

records.title: Concurrent Distributed Events
verifiedClaims: Two distributed events are concurrent under Lamport’s relation when neither event happens before the other.

sources.title: Leslie Lamport — Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

records.title: Raft Commit Majority
verifiedClaims: Raft commits entries from the current term when they are stored on a majority of servers under the protocol’s commitment rules.

sources.title: USENIX ATC 2014 — In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)

records.title: Raft Log Matching Property
verifiedClaims: Raft’s log-matching property ensures that if two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, the logs are identical through that index.

sources.title: USENIX ATC 2014 — In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)

records.title: Qubit State Vector
verifiedClaims: A pure qubit state can be represented by two complex amplitudes whose squared magnitudes sum to one.

records.title: Computational Basis Measurement
verifiedClaims: Measuring a qubit in the computational basis produces 0 or 1 with probabilities given by the squared magnitudes of the corresponding amplitudes.

records.title: Pauli Z Gate
verifiedClaims: The Pauli Z gate leaves |0⟩ unchanged and multiplies |1⟩ by -1, changing relative phase.

records.title: Quantum Tensor Product
verifiedClaims: The state space of multiple qubits is formed with tensor products, so two qubits are represented in a four-dimensional complex vector space.

records.title: Bell State
verifiedClaims: A Bell state is a maximally entangled two-qubit state with measurement correlations that cannot be represented as independent single-qubit pure states.

records.title: Quantum Circuit
verifiedClaims: A quantum circuit represents an ordered sequence of quantum operations and measurements applied to qubit registers.

records.title: Quantum Measurement Shots
verifiedClaims: On quantum hardware and shot-based simulators, repeated circuit executions produce a distribution of classical measurement outcomes.

records.title: Relative Phase
verifiedClaims: Relative phase between amplitudes can change interference and therefore affect later measurement probabilities.

records.title: Unitary Quantum Gate
verifiedClaims: Ideal closed-system quantum gates are represented by unitary operators that preserve state-vector norm.

records.title: Quantum Entanglement
verifiedClaims: Entangled states are joint multi-qubit states that cannot be written as a tensor product of individual subsystem states.

records.title: Quantum Interference
verifiedClaims: Quantum algorithms can combine amplitudes so some computational paths reinforce while others cancel before measurement.

records.title: Load-Store Architecture
verifiedClaims: RISC-V base integer instructions access memory through explicit load and store instructions while arithmetic instructions operate on registers.

records.title: Aligned Memory Access
verifiedClaims: Processor architectures define alignment behavior for memory operands; aligned access means the address satisfies the alignment requirement of the access size or instruction.

records.title: Little-Endian Byte Order
verifiedClaims: Little-endian systems store the least-significant byte of a multibyte integer at the lowest memory address.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Atomic Read-Modify-Write
verifiedClaims: Atomic read-modify-write instructions perform a memory update as one indivisible operation with architecture-defined ordering semantics.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Memory Fence
verifiedClaims: A memory fence constrains the ordering or visibility of memory operations according to an architecture’s memory model.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Cache Hit
verifiedClaims: A cache hit occurs when the requested memory block is present in the cache level being checked.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Cache Miss
verifiedClaims: A cache miss occurs when the requested memory block is absent from the cache level and must be obtained from another level of the memory hierarchy.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Memory Latency
verifiedClaims: Memory latency is the time between issuing a memory request and receiving the requested data or completion response.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Memory Bandwidth
verifiedClaims: Memory bandwidth describes the rate at which data can be transferred through a memory subsystem over time.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Working Set
verifiedClaims: A working set is the subset of code and data actively used during a phase of execution; performance can improve when the working set fits efficiently within faster levels of the memory hierarchy.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Data-Level Parallelism
verifiedClaims: Data-level parallelism exists when the same operation can be applied independently across multiple data elements, enabling SIMD or vector execution.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Thread-Level Parallelism
verifiedClaims: Thread-level parallelism executes multiple independent or partially independent instruction streams concurrently on cores or hardware thread contexts.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Vector Register
verifiedClaims: Vector or SIMD registers store multiple data elements so one instruction can operate on several elements at once.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Branch Misprediction
verifiedClaims: A branch misprediction occurs when speculative control-flow prediction is wrong and incorrectly fetched or executed work must be discarded before correct execution continues.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Pipeline Stall
verifiedClaims: A pipeline stall delays instruction progress because a required operand, resource, translation, or control decision is not yet available.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Micro-operations
verifiedClaims: Some complex machine instructions are decoded internally into one or more simpler micro-operations that the processor schedules and executes.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Retirement
verifiedClaims: Instruction retirement commits completed instruction results to the architectural state in program order on processors that support precise out-of-order execution.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: Hardware Multithreading
verifiedClaims: Hardware multithreading allows one physical core to maintain and schedule more than one architectural thread context.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual

records.title: Demand Paging
verifiedClaims: Demand paging brings a virtual page into physical memory when it is needed rather than requiring every mapped page to be resident in advance.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: Page Fault
verifiedClaims: A page fault occurs when address translation or access permissions require the operating system to handle a virtual-memory event before execution can continue.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: Dirty Page
verifiedClaims: A dirty page contains modified data that has not yet been synchronized to its backing storage and therefore must be written before the page can be safely discarded when persistence is required.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: Memory Compaction
verifiedClaims: Linux memory compaction moves movable pages to create larger physically contiguous free regions.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: OOM Killer
verifiedClaims: Linux can invoke the out-of-memory killer when memory cannot be reclaimed sufficiently to satisfy allocation demands, selecting processes for termination according to kernel policy.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: NUMA Memory Policy
verifiedClaims: Linux NUMA memory policy lets software influence which NUMA nodes are preferred or allowed for memory allocation.

sources.title: Linux Kernel Documentation — Memory Management Concepts

records.title: Page Table Hierarchy
verifiedClaims: Linux page tables are hierarchical structures whose levels progressively translate portions of a virtual address toward a physical page mapping.

records.title: TLB Miss
verifiedClaims: A TLB miss means the required virtual-to-physical translation is not present in the translation cache and another translation mechanism such as a page-table walk is required.

records.title: Page Walk Cache
verifiedClaims: Some processors cache intermediate page-table information in dedicated page-walk caches to reduce translation overhead.

records.title: Kernel Privilege
verifiedClaims: Operating systems execute privileged kernel code with access to processor facilities and memory that user-mode code cannot directly access.

sources.title: Intel — 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals

records.title: OpenMP static Schedule
verifiedClaims: An OpenMP static loop schedule assigns iteration chunks to threads before the loop executes according to the static scheduling rules.

records.title: OpenMP dynamic Schedule
verifiedClaims: An OpenMP dynamic loop schedule assigns chunks to threads as threads become available, enabling work redistribution during execution.

records.title: OpenMP guided Schedule
verifiedClaims: An OpenMP guided schedule assigns chunks dynamically while generally decreasing chunk sizes as work proceeds until a minimum chunk size is reached.

records.title: OpenMP nowait Clause
verifiedClaims: The OpenMP nowait clause removes the implicit barrier from constructs where the specification permits nowait.

records.title: OpenMP taskwait
verifiedClaims: OpenMP taskwait suspends the current task until specified child or dependent tasks complete according to taskwait semantics.

records.title: OpenMP task depend
verifiedClaims: OpenMP depend clauses express ordering dependencies between sibling tasks based on matching dependence information.

records.title: OpenMP collapse Clause
verifiedClaims: The OpenMP collapse clause associates multiple nested loops with a loop directive so their iteration spaces are combined according to specification rules.

records.title: OpenMP firstprivate
verifiedClaims: OpenMP firstprivate gives each task or thread a private copy initialized from the original variable’s value before the region executes.

records.title: OpenMP lastprivate
verifiedClaims: OpenMP lastprivate can copy the value from the logically last iteration or section back to the original variable according to directive semantics.

records.title: MPI Allgather
verifiedClaims: MPI_Allgather gathers each process contribution and distributes the complete gathered result to every participating process.

records.title: MPI Alltoall
verifiedClaims: MPI_Alltoall performs a personalized all-to-all exchange in which each process sends a distinct block to every other process.

records.title: MPI Reduce_scatter
verifiedClaims: MPI_Reduce_scatter reduces distributed values and scatters portions of the reduced result among participating processes.

records.title: MPI Scan
verifiedClaims: MPI_Scan performs an inclusive prefix reduction so each process receives the reduction of values from lower ranks through its own rank.

records.title: MPI Exclusive Scan
verifiedClaims: MPI_Exscan performs an exclusive prefix reduction in which each process receives the reduction of values from lower ranks, excluding its own contribution.

records.title: MPI Probe
verifiedClaims: MPI_Probe lets a process inspect an incoming matching message status before receiving the message payload.

records.title: MPI ANY_SOURCE
verifiedClaims: MPI_ANY_SOURCE can be used in a receive to accept a matching message from any source rank in the communicator.

records.title: MPI ANY_TAG
verifiedClaims: MPI_ANY_TAG can be used in a receive to accept a matching message with any tag.

records.title: MPI Derived Datatype
verifiedClaims: MPI derived datatypes describe noncontiguous or structured memory layouts so communication routines can transfer logical data structures without manual packing in many cases.

records.title: MPI Cartesian Topology
verifiedClaims: MPI supports Cartesian virtual topologies that map ranks into multidimensional grids and provide topology-aware rank-coordinate helpers.

records.title: CUDA blockIdx

records.title: CUDA threadIdx
verifiedClaims: CUDA exposes threadIdx so device code can identify a thread’s index within its block.

records.title: CUDA blockDim

records.title: CUDA gridDim
verifiedClaims: CUDA exposes gridDim so device code can determine the dimensions of the launched grid.

records.title: CUDA Memory Transaction
verifiedClaims: CUDA global-memory requests from threads in a warp are serviced with memory transactions covering the required address segments.

records.title: CUDA Shared-Memory Bank Conflicts
verifiedClaims: Shared-memory accesses can serialize when multiple threads in a warp contend for the same memory bank under access patterns that create bank conflicts.

records.title: CUDA Pinned Host Memory
verifiedClaims: Page-locked host memory can improve host-device transfer behavior and is required for some forms of truly asynchronous host-device memory copy.

records.title: CUDA Asynchronous Copy

records.title: CUDA Event
